items.heading: Overview
items.paragraph:
This course will address many of the challenges inherent in expanding AI throughout your organization, including an overview of the skills and talent needed to implement these technologies and a discussion of risk management, data quality, and related ethical issues. We will focus on the talent needs for your organization and evaluate different strategies to attract and train talent. We will also learn the importance of AI risk management and assess the unique risks posed by Generative AI.

If you haven’t yet taken the first course in this series, Designing AI Projects in Government, we highly recommend you do so,  as it focuses on understanding different types of AI and identifying the right AI projects for your organization.

After each video ends, a continue button appears below the video player. Click it to reveal the additional navigation and the InnovateUS website link containing readings and resources. Learners with screen readers can use the down arrow key to navigate through the video player’s controls and access the continue button. Another “continue” button will appear to move on to the Self-Assessments after each video.

  • Reminder: Consult with your organization’s policies before using any tool or platform.  

  • Disclaimer: The commercial tools mentioned in this course are for illustrative purposes and do not imply endorsement by InnovateUS.

items.title: When considering an AI project, a department should:

answers.title: Assume their data is too messy or incomplete and not pursue the project
answers.feedback: Departments should assess data fitness for the specific purpose before deciding not to pursue an AI project.

answers.title: Assess the fitness of their data for the specific purpose of the AI project
answers.feedback: The correct answer is B. Departments should assess the fitness of their data for the specific purpose of the AI project before deciding whether to proceed.

answers.title: Proceed with the AI project regardless of data quality concerns
answers.feedback: Proceeding without assessing data quality can lead to inaccurate AI outputs and unintended consequences.

answers.title: Wait until they have perfect data before considering any AI projects
answers.feedback: Perfect data is not necessary; data should be assessed for fitness for the specific purpose.

items.heading: Heading
items.paragraph: This video explores the impact of data quality issues on AI projects, highlighting how poor data quality can lead to wasted staff hours and wrong conclusions. It explains how AI systems are more sensitive to data quality problems and can propagate the impact of those problems more widely and rapidly compared to non-AI projects. The video also discusses how AI can amplify existing biases in the data, leading to discriminatory outcomes, and emphasizes the importance of addressing data quality issues to ensure responsible and ethical AI deployment.

items.title: Why is labeled data essential for supervised learning in machine learning-based AI models?

answers.title: Labeled data helps the model learn to make accurate predictions or decisions
answers.feedback: Labeled data is essential for training machine learning-based AI models because it helps the model learn to make accurate predictions or decisions.

answers.title: Labeled data is easier to collect than unlabeled data
answers.feedback: Labeled data is often more challenging to collect than unlabeled data, as it requires human annotation.

answers.title: Labeled data ensures the model's outputs are always unbiased
answers.feedback: While labeled data is important, it does not guarantee unbiased model outputs, as bias can still be present in the labels or the data itself.

answers.title: Labeled data is required for all types of AI models
answers.feedback: Labeled data is particularly important for machine learning-based AI models, but not all types of AI models require labeled data.

items.title: Which of the following are potential consequences of AI models amplifying biases in data? Select all that apply.

answers.title: Unfair treatment of individuals based on protected characteristic
Perpetuation of historical inequities and discrimination
Reduction in AI model accuracy and reliability
Increased public trust in AI-based decision-making

items.feedbackCorrect: The correct answers are A, B, and C. AI models amplifying biases in data can lead to unfair treatment of individuals based on protected characteristics, perpetuation of historical inequities and discrimination, and reduction in AI model accuracy and reliability.
items.feedbackIncorrect: It does not increase public trust in AI-based decision-making.

items.title: What role can a Chief Data Officer or Director of Data and Research play in AI projects?

answers.title: Acting as a cultural bridge between IT and program units
answers.feedback: A Chief Data Officer or Director of Data and Research can play a key role in AI projects by acting as a cultural bridge between IT and program units.

answers.title: Ensuring that AI projects only focus on data-related issues
answers.feedback: AI projects should consider a wide range of factors beyond just data-related issues.

answers.title: Replacing the need for IT involvement in AI projects
answers.feedback: IT involvement is still crucial for AI projects, even with a Chief Data Officer or Director of Data and Research.

answers.title: Guaranteeing the success of all AI projects
answers.feedback: While a Chief Data Officer or Director of Data and Research can help facilitate success, they cannot guarantee the success of all AI projects.

items.title: What should be done before starting or funding major AI projects?

answers.title: Allocate parallel resources for ongoing data quality efforts
answers.feedback: Before starting or funding major AI projects, parallel resources should be allocated for ongoing data quality efforts.

answers.title: Ignore data quality considerations and focus solely on AI development
answers.feedback: Data quality considerations should be addressed in parallel with AI development, not ignored.

answers.title: Postpone data governance efforts until after AI projects are completed
answers.feedback: Data governance efforts should be undertaken before and during AI projects, not postponed until after completion.

answers.title: Rely on existing resources without additional allocation for data quality
answers.feedback: Additional resources should be allocated for data quality efforts, rather than solely relying on existing resources.

items.title: What is the benefit of focusing on key datasets for AI projects?

answers.title: It allows the project team to ignore data quality issues
answers.feedback: Focusing on key datasets does not mean ignoring data quality issues; rather, it allows for targeted efforts to address quality issues in the most critical data.

answers.title: It ensures that all available data is used, regardless of relevance
answers.feedback: Focusing on key datasets involves prioritizing the most relevant data, not using all available data regardless of relevance.

answers.title: It enables targeted efforts to improve data quality for the most critical data
answers.feedback: The benefit of focusing on key datasets for AI projects is that it enables targeted efforts to improve data quality for the most critical data.

answers.title: It eliminates the need for stakeholder involvement in data quality efforts
answers.feedback: Focusing on key datasets does not eliminate the need for stakeholder involvement; in fact, stakeholder alignment is crucial for ensuring data quality in these critical datasets.

answers.feedback: Focusing too narrowly on a few risk areas may not improve fairness and transparency if other relevant characteristics are ignored

items.title: According to the NIST AI Risk Management Framework, which of the following are characteristics of accountable and transparent AI? (Select all that apply)

answers.title: How an AI decision system is used should be made transparent to users
It should be clear who is responsible for the outcomes of using the AI system
The AI system should be able to explain its decision-making process in detail
The AI system should be able to make decisions without human oversight

items.feedbackIncorrect: According to the NIST AI Risk Management Framework, the characteristics of accountable and transparent AI are that how an AI decision system is used should be made transparent to users, and it should be clear who is responsible for the outcomes of using the system. Explainability is a separate characteristic, and accountability and transparency do not imply that AI systems should make decisions without human oversight.

items.heading: Heading
items.paragraph: This video discusses the four functions (Govern, Map, Measure, and Manage) outlined in the AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF) that can help reduce risk and maximize benefits in each of the seven characteristics of trustworthy AI. It explains how the Govern function focuses on establishing the ecosystem for the other three functions to succeed, while Map, Measure, and Manage are iterative steps for managing risk throughout the AI lifecycle. The video also emphasizes the importance of tailoring the AI RMF activities to an organization's specific context and treating the framework as a tool for thinking and judicious action rather than a checklist.

items.title: According to the recommendations in the module, which of the following are practical steps to embed AI risk management in an organization? (Select all that apply)

answers.title: Designate an AI risk champion
Commit to regularly evaluating AI systems for common patterns of bias
Identify practical toolkits and guides that operationalize the concepts in the AI RMF
Invest in deeper AI risk management education
Assign AI risk mitigation exclusively to lawyers or privacy officers

items.feedbackIncorrect: According to the recommendations in the module, practical steps to embed AI risk management in an organization include designating an AI risk champion, committing to regularly evaluating AI systems for common patterns of bias, identifying practical toolkits and guides that operationalize the concepts in the AI RMF, and investing in deeper AI risk management education. The module does not recommend assigning AI risk mitigation exclusively to lawyers or privacy officers who may lack the requisite training in these new tools.

items.heading: Heading
items.paragraph: The conclusion video summarizes the key learning points from the course, including understanding different AI approaches, selecting and prioritizing impactful AI projects, ensuring data quality, developing an AI-ready workforce, and navigating ethical considerations and risk management practices. It emphasizes the importance of focusing on solving real problems, maintaining transparency, minimizing and managing AI risk, and prioritizing the public good. The video also highlights the crucial role of government leaders in shaping the future of AI in the public sector and the importance of continuous learning, collaboration, and adaptation to navigate the evolving AI landscape with confidence.

description:
This course will address many of the challenges inherent in expanding AI throughout your organization, including an overview of the skills and talent needed to implement these technologies and a discussion of risk management, data quality, and related ethical issues. We will focus on the talent needs for your organization and evaluate different strategies to attract and train talent. We will also learn the importance of AI risk management and assess the unique risks posed by Generative AI.
